**`crimes context` didn't help here.** It treated the parent `/Users/andrew/dev/crimes` repo as the root, and that repo's config excludes `evals/`. So the tag was never analysed: `analysis_status: "not_analyzed"`, a `working_set_path_unmatched` warning, and `related_files: []`. That empty list doesn't mean the tag has no callers. I found them by grepping the fixture instead.

## Pages that call `inputField.tag` (9 calls in 3 files)

| Page | Line | Call |
|---|---|---|
| `src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/jsp/owners/createOrUpdateOwnerForm.jsp` | 15–19 | firstName, lastName, address, city, telephone |
| `src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/jsp/pets/createOrUpdatePetForm.jsp` | 29–30 | name, birthDate |
| `src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/jsp/pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.jsp` | 39–40 | date, description |

All 9 calls pass only `label` and `name`. A new required `placeholder` would break every one of them, and therefore all three forms.

## How the pages reach the tag

Each page has `<%@ taglib prefix="petclinic" tagdir="/WEB-INF/tags" %>` and calls `<petclinic:inputField …/>`. Because it's a tag file found by `tagdir`, with no `.tld`, `.tagx` or `web.xml` entry, the tag name comes straight from the file name. Nothing checks the attributes until Jasper translates the page.

The same import appears in `welcome.jsp`, `vetList.jsp`, `ownerDetails.jsp`, `exception.jsp`, `ownersList.jsp`, `findOwners.jsp`, and in the `menu`, `bodyHeader` and `layout` tags. None of those calls `inputField`, so they're unaffected. I also searched for the bare string `inputField` across `src/` and `pom.xml`: the 9 calls above are the only hits.

## What I'd check before shipping

1. **Make it optional, or update all 9 calls in the same change.** `required="false"` plus `<c:if test="${not empty placeholder}">` avoids any breakage. If it must be required, fix every call above together.
2. **Nothing in the build catches this.** `pom.xml` has `tomcat-jasper-el` but no JSP precompile step (no jspc/jasper plugin). Spring MockMvc tests don't render JSPs either, so they'll pass whatever the attribute says. Either add precompilation, or test against a running server: request `/owners/new`, `/owners/{id}/edit`, `/owners/{id}/pets/new`, `/owners/{id}/pets/{petId}/edit` and `/owners/{id}/pets/{petId}/visits/new`, and confirm each one renders.
3. **`spring:bind` and `form:input` inside the tag.** `placeholder` has to be passed to `<form:input>`, which accepts it as a normal HTML attribute. Check the escaping if placeholder text could ever come from data.
4. **`selectField.tag`** follows the same pattern. Decide whether it should get `placeholder` too, so the two stay consistent.
5. **Date fields** (`birthDate`, visit `date`) need a format hint such as `yyyy-MM-dd`, not just a label. That's the main reason to add this attribute.
6. **Fix crimes for this fixture.** Run it with the fixture as its own root (for example from inside the fixture with its own config), or remove `evals/` from the parent repo's `exclude`. Otherwise `context` will keep returning nothing for these files.
